scope: Karaman core - Larende, Konya, Beysehir, Seydisehir, Bozkir, Hadim corridor
sources: Sait Kofoğlu, A Principality In Southwest Anatolia In The Post-Selçuk Era: Eşrefoğullari, SDÜ Sosyal Bilimler Dergisi 19 (2009)
Selçuk Üniversitesi Selçuklu Araştırmaları Dergisi: Konya-Alanya güzergâhındaki Selçuklu kervansarayları ve Eşrefoğlu Beyliği

Larende_Karaman.notes: Karamanid capital from Ibrahim Bey's period; the dynasty's central seat was Larende. Do not project later provincial boundaries onto 1326.

Konya.notes: Demirtas captured Konya in 1320 and 1323; after his withdrawal the Karamanids regained it only in 1328-29. Therefore Konya must not be encoded as a stable Karamanid polygon on 1326-04-07.

Beysehir.notes: Eshrefid II Suleyman was killed at Beysehir on 1326-10-09. TDV says Beysehir and surrounding Eshrefid lands were subsequently seized by Hamidids. This is later than the scenario start, so 7 April must remain unresolved rather than back-projecting October control.

Seydisehir.control: Eshrefid / transition zone at scenario start
Seydisehir.notes: TDV places Seydisehir under Eshrefids, then Hamidids, Karamanids and later Turgutids. The decisive Eshrefid collapse is October 1326, so no later Hamidid control should be back-projected to April.

Bozkir.control: Eshrefid legacy / frontier, not safely Karamanid in April 1326
Bozkir.notes: Eshrefid territory had historically extended south to Bozkir. Later Karamanid association is real, but the available sources do not establish an exact 7 April 1326 boundary.

Hadim.control: Karamanid-associated southern corridor, exact April 1326 boundary unresolved
Hadim.notes: Modern historical studies place Hadim in the Karamanid period and identify the Hadim-Bozkir route as a major Toros transit corridor. Exact 1326 political geometry is not established.

chronologyGuards: Do not assign Beysehir/Seydisehir to Hamidids before the documented 9 October 1326 Eshrefid collapse.
Do not assign Konya as stable Karamanid in April 1326; the documented Karamanid recovery is 1328-29.
Do not use later Karamanid provincial boundaries as 1326 polygons.
Separate city control, dynastic influence, route control and frontier pressure.
Treat the Konya-Alanya road as a transport network independent of political polygons.

Konya_Alanya_corridor.notes: Academic research identifies the Konya-Beysehir-Alanya/Akdeniz route as a major medieval caravan corridor; Beysehir's strategic position connected inland Anatolia to Mediterranean ports.

Anamur_Ermenek_Hadim_Bozkir_Seydisehir.notes: Academic route reconstruction identifies a southern route from Anamur through Ermenek, Kisle, Taşkent, Hadim, Bozkir and south of Lake Sugla toward Seydisehir. This supports a route-network layer, not an automatic political boundary.

inferencePolicy: Where sources establish a later 1326 transition but not the exact scenario date, retain unresolved/transition state instead of back-projecting the later result.
